title: Numbers, age & quantities
goal: Count things and people, ask 'how many / how much', give your age, use ordinals and the everyday fractions (दीड, अडीच, साडे…).
intro:
Marathi numbers 1–100 must largely be learned one by one (see the **Numbers** chart): 25 is पंचवीस, 26 सव्वीस, 29 एकोणतीस ('one-less-thirty'). Start with 1–20 and the tens, then fill in the rest.

Just as important in daily life are the special fraction words: **दीड** (1½), **अडीच** (2½), and the prefixes **साडे-** (+½), **सव्वा-** (+¼) and **पावणे-** (−¼). You'll use them for time, money and weights constantly.

vocab.note: f कितवी: ती कितवीत आहे? 'Which class (standard) is she in?'
n · pl: वर्षं · '… years old' = … वर्षांचा (m) / वर्षांची (f)
पाव किलो 'a quarter kilo'. (Also पाव = bread roll, as in वडापाव!)
f सगळी, n सगळं, pl सगळे 'everyone'
Used after numbers: चार जण 'four people'; f जणी for women: तीन जणी.

phrases.en: How many of you are there?
How much does it come to?
Give me two kilos of tomatoes.
I live on the third floor. (man)

grammar.title: Counting nouns and people
grammar.body:
After a number above one, the noun is **plural**: एक आंबा, दोन आंबे; एक मुलगी, तीन मुली; एक घर, चार घरं.

For people, Marathi often adds the counting word **जण** (m / mixed) or **जणी** (all women): पाच जण 'five people', आम्ही तिघी जणी 'we three women'. 'Both / all three' have special forms: दोघं (both), तिघं (all three), चौघं (all four).

The fractions combine directly with numbers and units: **दीड** किलो 1½ kg, **अडीच** लिटर 2½ litres, **साडे**तीन वर्षं 3½ years, **सव्वा**शे 125, **पावणे**दोन 1¾.

examples.en: There are thirty people in the class.
one and a half kilos of sugar

grammar.title: Asking quantity and age
grammar.body:
**किती** asks 'how many / how much' and never changes. Put it before the noun or the verb.

For age, either ask तुमचं **वय** किती आहे? ('what is your age?') or तुम्ही किती **वर्षांचे** आहात? ('of how many years are you?'). The answer uses वर्षांचा / वर्षांची / वर्षांचं, agreeing with the person: मी तीस वर्षांचा आहे (man), मी तीस वर्षांची आहे (woman), बाळ एक वर्षाचं आहे (the baby, neuter).

**कितवा** asks about position in a sequence: तुम्ही कितव्या मजल्यावर राहता? 'Which floor do you live on?'

examples.en: How much money do you have?
The baby is six months old.
Which floor do you live on?

dialogue.title: A birthday party
dialogue.setting: Meera chats with her friend Neha, who is preparing for her daughter's birthday.

lines.speaker: Neha
lines.native: ती सात वर्षांची आहे. आज तिचा वाढदिवस आहे!
lines.roman: tī sāt varṣānchī āhe. ādz titsā vāḍhdivas āhe!
lines.en: She's seven. It's her birthday today!

lines.speaker: Meera
lines.en: Oh lovely! Which class is she in?

lines.speaker: Neha
lines.en: Second. And my son is in fifth.

lines.speaker: Meera
lines.en: How many people are coming to the party?

lines.speaker: Neha
lines.native: वीस-पंचवीस मुलं. आणि त्यांचे आई-वडील पण!
lines.roman: vīs-pantsvīs mulaṃ. āṇi tyānche āī-vaḍīl paṇ!
lines.en: Twenty or twenty-five kids. And their parents too!

lines.speaker: Meera
lines.en: Goodness! That's a lot of people.

lines.speaker: Neha
lines.native: हो ना. मी तीस समोसे आणि दोन केक आणले आहेत.
lines.roman: ho nā. mī tīs samose āṇi don kek āṇle āhet.
lines.en: I know. I've brought thirty samosas and two cakes.

culture: In Maharashtra, school years are called by ordinal number in the feminine: पहिली, दुसरी … दहावी, बारावी (the 10th and 12th standard board exams, **दहावी** and **बारावी**, are major life events). Large numbers are counted in **लाख** (100,000) and **कोटी** (10 million), written १,००,००० — never in millions. And when a price or time is 'one-and-a-half' or 'quarter-to', expect दीड, सव्वा, पावणे — even in Mumbai English ('dedh sau' becomes 'दीडशे').
